posts.angle: Separate the live-mix problem from the next-session memory problem
posts.headline: The miniature-painting gift that solves two different losses
posts.copy: A wet palette can keep one conventional-acrylic mix workable today. A labeled dry swatch can make it reproducible next session. The thoughtful gift is the loop—only after you verify both problems are real.
posts.assetBrief: Original vertical diagram showing one live acrylic mix moving from palette to miniature, then a tiny swatch and four-field recipe record; no logos or product photography.
posts.altText: Diagram showing a live acrylic mix on a wet palette and the same mix recorded as a labeled dry swatch for a later painting session.

posts.angle: Make paint-medium compatibility the first gift check
posts.headline: Ask this before gifting a miniature painter a wet palette
posts.copy: Do they mix conventional water-based acrylics? Stop if the workflow is mainly oils, enamels, airbrush-only, or one-coat paints that need a hard palette. The hobby label is not enough; the paint medium decides the tool.
posts.assetBrief: Original compatibility checklist with conventional acrylic as the proceed branch and oils, enamels, airbrush-only, and Speedpaint-style workflows as stop-and-ask branches.
posts.altText: Checklist asking whether a miniature painter uses conventional water-based acrylics before choosing a wet palette.

posts.angle: Turn recipe logging into one tiny repeatable action
posts.headline: A paint recipe is more than a photo of the palette
posts.copy: Record four things before cleanup: paint brand and name, approximate drop ratio, model area, and layer order. Add one small dried swatch. That is enough to make the next matching unit less of a guessing game.
posts.assetBrief: Original blank recipe-card graphic with four text fields and one dried-swatch box, using generic color dots and no third-party designs.
posts.altText: Blank miniature paint recipe card with fields for paint names, ratio, model area, layer order, and a dried swatch.

posts.angle: Show the compact desk pair as a five-minute cleanup ritual
posts.headline: Keep the mix today. Remember the recipe next session.
posts.copy: Slide through the compact desk loop: hydrate one ordinary acrylic mix, paint the unit, write the model area and ratio, add a tiny swatch, then let the page dry flat. Buy only one half if the other step will not happen.
posts.assetBrief: Six original illustrated slides: observed problem, palette role, journal role, five-line key, compatibility stop signs, and choose-one fallback; no merchant imagery.
posts.altText: Carousel explaining a compact miniature-painting routine from hydrated acrylic mix to a written recipe and dried color swatch.

posts.angle: Make the reason to buy only the anchor as prominent as the bundle
posts.headline: When the thoughtful miniature-painting pair should be one gift
posts.copy: Choose one palette configuration, never both: roomier Redgrass with reusable membranes, or compact Army Painter with brush storage. Both use the same qualified Strathmore record. Buy only the palette if they dislike logging; buy only the journal if their current palette works.
posts.assetBrief: Original three-column decision card labeled Pair, Anchor only, and Skip, with simple palette and notebook line icons.
posts.altText: Decision card showing when to buy a wet palette and recipe journal together, when to buy one item, and when to skip both.

posts.angle: Open with the failed color match and reveal the two-part workflow
posts.headline: Why the next squad never matches the first one
posts.copy: Hook: the perfect armor mix dried, and the photo never captured the ratio. Show a generic acrylic mix, a later mismatched model, then the fix: keep the mix workable now and log four fields plus a dry swatch for next time. End with the paint-medium check.
posts.assetBrief: Original staged storyboard with generic unbranded miniatures, paint dots, palette surface, handwritten card, and an explicit no-hands-on-performance-claim caption.
posts.altText: Short video storyboard showing a lost acrylic mix, a mismatched later miniature, and a simple palette-to-recipe-card routine.
